title: Cross-sectional telomere study and machine-learning analysis in adults with type 2 diabetes after COVID-19
summary: In a cross-sectional pilot of adults with type 2 diabetes, leukocyte telomere length was shorter among those with post-COVID syndrome than those without it. Machine-learning models were also evaluated for identifying syndrome status; this observational association does not establish telomere shortening as a cause.
ai_technology: Machine-learning classification of post-COVID syndrome using clinical and telomere-related variables.
organization: Bogomolets National Medical University; Institute of Gerontology, National Academy of Medical Sciences of Ukraine

evidence.tested: Cross-sectional groups comprised 44 participants with post-COVID syndrome and 22 without; mean telomere length was 1.09±0.19 versus 1.28±0.24 (p=.001); reported gradient-boosting AUC was .753.
evidence.unknown: Single-center pilot, cross-sectional association and model evaluation; no causal inference or prospective clinical benefit established.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning classification of post-COVID syndrome using clinical and telomere-related variables.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
